placements.why: The document is a self-contained calibration report — an instrument, a measured value, and a verification act against named reference standards — with no existing strata category to hold it. Nothing in an empty strata tier (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates or any other) covers instrument-verification work; the content itself names a distinct organizational activity (checking a claim against a physical/reference standard) that future calibration envelopes for other instruments would keep feeding. Minted standalone since nothing existing is even close.
placements.title: Instrument calibration and verification work becomes its own organizational category
placements.frame: What instrument, calibration value, and reference standard does this verification record establish or revisit?

placements.title: An instrument's calibration is trustworthy because it was checked against a named reference standard
placements.frame: What reference standard was this calibration verified against, and does the verification hold across the full range being claimed?
placements.why: All three segments carry the same directional content — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is asserted and grounded by verification against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band — src-1 in narrative prose, src-2/src-3 as labelled-field restatement of the identical claim. This is a recurring subject, not a one-time fact: the specific value (88.4 MHz) and specific standard (June reference plates) are position-grain evidence, but the underlying theme — calibration claims are earned through verification against a named reference, not asserted bare — is exactly the kind of subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets) would keep feeding. The graph structure is empty, so nothing exists to reuse; minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata since no hub or leaf was available to hold it.
